title: Realization weak equivalences tested by Kan targets
statement:
Use simplicial sets, geometric realization, Kan complexes and the internal functor simplicial set of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe. For any simplicial set $T$, let $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(T)$ be its vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by the pairs of endpoints of its edges. For every simplicial map $v:P\to Q$, the following are equivalent: (i) $|v|$ induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group; (ii) for every Kan complex $W$ in that universe, precomposition induces a bijection
$$\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(\operatorname{Fun}(Q,W))\longrightarrow\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(\operatorname{Fun}(P,W)).$$
No Kan condition on $P$ or $Q$, nonemptiness condition, or injectivity condition on $v$ is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 3.6.4.3 (Tag 03X7), equivalence of (1) and (2): condition (2) is the realization condition; condition (1) is the Kan-target testing condition of Definition 3.1.7.12 (Tag 00UA). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Assume (i) and put $f=|v|$. The nondegenerate-simplex description [lem-cbc-realization-cw-subcomplex] gives the CW structures on $|P|$ and $|Q|$: use one open $n$-cell per nondegenerate $n$-simplex, attach its closed simplex along the faces, and replace a degenerate face by its nondegenerate representative. Each boundary meets only the finitely many faces and their iterated faces. The characteristic-map closed-set criterion is precisely the weak topology of these cell attachments. The standard closed simplex is a disk with boundary sphere by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-cbc-whitehead-cw-homotopy-inverse] hold for $f$; choose a continuous $h:|Q|\to|P|$ with $hf\simeq1$ and $fh\simeq1$.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.4.3, implication (2) to (3); Remark 1.2.3.12 for the cells

proof.text: For every Kan $W$, use [lem-cbc-kan-realization-mapping-classes] with $K=P,Q$. It identifies the precomposition map in (ii) with $f^*:[|Q|,|W|]_{\mathrm{top}}\to[|P|,|W|]_{\mathrm{top}}$. Precomposition with $h$ is inverse: the equations $hf\simeq1$ and $fh\simeq1$ remain homotopies after composition with any continuous map to $|W|$. Hence $f^*$, and therefore the required map, is bijective. This proves (i) implies (ii).

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2, naturality of the comparison on components

proof.text: For the converse use the following explicit test objects. For a k-space $T$ in the category of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] let $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$, with simplicial operators given by precomposition. The realization--singular adjunction of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] shows that a horn into $\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ is a continuous map $|\Lambda_i^n|\to T$. The same node identifies the realized horn pair with $(D^{n-1}\times[0,1],D^{n-1}\times\{0\})$. Projection onto the second member is a retraction; precomposing the horn map with this retraction extends it over $|\Delta^n|$. Thus $\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ is Kan, for every such $T$, including the empty space.

source.place: Singular-complex test expanded using realized horn retractions

proof.text: For every simplicial $K$ the same adjunction identifies maps $a:K\to\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ with continuous maps $\bar a:|K|\to T$. This descends, naturally in $K,T$, to a bijection $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Sing}(T))\cong[|K|,T]_{\mathrm{top}}$. Here are the homotopy details. An edge on the left is a map $K\times\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Sing}(T)$, whose adjoint is a continuous map $|K\times\Delta^1|\to T$. Finite-product preservation of realization [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] and compact-open currying [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] identify this with a continuous homotopy on $|K|\times[0,1]$. To check the ordinary-product topology explicitly, a homotopy on each characteristic simplex transposes to a map $|\Delta^m|\to\operatorname{Cont}([0,1],T)$; compatible transposes descend continuously to $|K|$ by its quotient topology, and evaluation is continuous because $[0,1]$ is compact and locally compact. Conversely, a continuous homotopy $G:|K|\times[0,1]\to T$ supplies the singular simplex associated to $(k,\alpha)\in(K\times\Delta^1)_m$ by $t\mapsto G(q_k(t),|\alpha|(t))$. These formulas commute with simplicial operators and have the prescribed endpoints. Finally finite edge zigzags yield homotopies by reversing and concatenating intervals, and an ordinary homotopy gives a single edge by the displayed formula. This proves injectivity as well as surjectivity of the asserted class bijection.

source.place: Proof, Example 3.6.2.5; adjunction on homotopies written out

proof.text: Assume (ii) and put $f=|v|$. By steps 3--4, for every k-space $T$ in the universe the Kan test $W=\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ gives a bijection $f^*:[|Q|,T]_{\mathrm{top}}\to[|P|,T]_{\mathrm{top}}$. The realizations $|P|$ and $|Q|$ are k-spaces by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Take $T=|P|$: surjectivity gives a continuous $h:|Q|\to|P|$ with $[hf]=[1_{|P|}]$. Take $T=|Q|$: the classes of $fh$ and $1_{|Q|}$ have equal precompositions with $f$, since $[fhf]=[f]$. Injectivity now gives $[fh]=[1_{|Q|}]$. These are actual continuous homotopies by the definition of the displayed class sets. Both tests fit in the fixed universe: realization is a quotient of a small coproduct of standard simplices and the singular complex consists of sets of maps between small sets. No choice of an inverse $Q\to P$ of simplicial sets has been asserted.

source.place: Converse, expanded two-target argument through the singular adjunction

proof.text: The maps $f,h$ of step 5 satisfy both hypotheses of [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. It follows that $f$ induces a bijection on path components and an isomorphism on every homotopy group at every source basepoint, even though its inverse homotopies need not fix basepoints. This is (i). If $P$ is empty and $Q$ is not, (ii) already fails for the empty Kan target; if $Q$ is empty a map $P\to Q$ forces $P$ empty. Thus the argument also covers all empty cases without adding hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Realization comparison proof using Proposition 3.6.5.2 and topological Whitehead; converse expanded by singular-complex tests and the two-target inverse argument. External sources read online, not archived in literature/.
